title: HDFC Bank Chairman Rajiv Kumar Pledges Zero Tolerance at AGM as Governance Reset Takes Shape
excerpt: Former finance secretary tells shareholders the board will enforce accountability, while management projects CASA and NIM improvement as legacy HDFC Ltd borrowings mature.
body:
• Former finance secretary Rajiv Kumar, now HDFC Bank's RBI-approved chairman, told shareholders at the August 5 AGM that the board will enforce "zero tolerance" for unethical practices.
  • Kumar's appointment follows the March resignation of predecessor Atanu Chakraborty and an independent legal review that found no evidence to support governance allegations.
  • Management projected improvement in the current-account savings-account (CASA) ratio and net interest margin (NIM) as high-cost legacy HDFC Ltd borrowings mature over the next two to three years.
  • CEO Sashidhar Jagdishan's reappointment is due before his October 26 term-end, a decision analysts call the next key governance milestone.

HDFC Bank's newly installed chairman Rajiv Kumar used the lender's annual general meeting on Tuesday to draw a line under months of governance turmoil, pledging accountability at India's largest private bank and outlining a path to stronger profitability metrics.

Zero Tolerance Pledge

Kumar, a 1984-batch IAS officer who previously served as India's chief election commissioner and financial services secretary, secured Reserve Bank of India approval for a three-year term in July. At the AGM, he told shareholders the board would maintain "zero tolerance for unethical practices," according to The Indian Express.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=xfQUS0_7Qjc

"The board will have zero tolerance for unethical practices."

— Rajiv Kumar, Chairman, HDFC Bank

The statement was a direct attempt to address investor anxiety that has hammered the stock. HDFC Bank shares have fallen roughly 20% in 2026, sharply underperforming the Nifty Private Bank index's 3% decline, according to Livemint.

Background: A Turbulent Six Months

The governance crisis began in March when former chairman Atanu Chakraborty, a retired Gujarat-cadre IAS officer, resigned citing concerns over "certain happenings and practices within the bank." The departure triggered a board-level review and intensified market scrutiny of the lender's internal controls.

An independent legal review subsequently found no evidence to support Chakraborty's allegations. The board appointed interim chairman Keki Mistry while conducting a search for a permanent replacement, eventually settling on Kumar in late June. The RBI formally approved his appointment on July 15, according to a regulatory filing by the bank.

CASA and NIM Recovery Roadmap

Beyond governance, CEO Sashidhar Jagdishan struck an optimistic tone at the AGM, telling shareholders the "next three years will be very exciting for the lender," according to Fortune India.

The bank's core challenge remains the legacy of its 2023 merger with HDFC Ltd, which loaded the balance sheet with high-cost borrowings that compress margins. Management outlined several levers for recovery:

Between ₹40,000 crore and ₹50,000 crore in high-cost borrowings are expected to mature over the next two to three years. Replacing them with retail term deposits could reduce the cost of funds by 100 to 125 basis points, analysts at Livemint noted.

About 40% of HDFC Bank's 9,700 branches are less than five years old. As these younger branches build their deposit base, the CASA ratio — currently around 32% versus ICICI Bank's 40% — is expected to improve, further lowering funding costs.

Management also signaled plans to expand the share of higher-yielding retail loans from 52% to 60%, a shift that could meaningfully narrow the NIM gap with rivals over the medium term.

What Investors Are Watching

Analysts say the most consequential governance event is still ahead. Jagdishan's current term as managing director and CEO expires on October 26, and the board's decision on his reappointment will serve as a litmus test for whether the bank's governance reset is substantive or cosmetic.

Nuvama values HDFC Bank at 2x FY28 book value, a significant discount to ICICI Bank's 2.5x multiple. Jefferies has maintained a bullish stance, suggesting the governance discount should narrow as leadership uncertainty resolves.

Diaspora Lens

HDFC Bank remains one of the most widely held Indian equities among NRI investors. The stock's 20% decline in 2026 has eroded significant portfolio value for overseas shareholders who viewed it as a blue-chip anchor. The resolution of governance concerns and a clearer margin trajectory will be closely watched by diaspora investors weighing whether to hold or add to positions.

What's Next

The immediate focus shifts to the board's decision on Jagdishan's reappointment before October and the quarterly earnings trajectory. If the bank can demonstrate a sustained improvement in CASA and NIM while maintaining clean governance signals under Kumar's watch, the valuation discount may begin to close.
